analysis.meta: These notes describe the published syllabus and the question types it implies. They are not a statistical count of past papers.

often: Sree Narayana Guru and the SNDP
types: Name-to-event matching: which reformer did this
Which year a movement or organisation began
bySubject.tip: A single timeline from Aruvippuram in 1888 to the 1936 proclamation answers most of this section.

types: Which body elects or appoints whom
bySubject.tip: Learn articles as numbers, not as descriptions: 14, 17, 19, 21A, 32, 40, 44, 51A, 123, 368.

types: Map-based questions on districts and passes
bySubject.tip: Fix the map first: districts, then rivers, then hills. Facts stick to a place better than to a list.
Most questions here are one-line recall, so revision beats practice; keep a short list of units and symbols.
Answers are usually friendly numbers. If your arithmetic gets messy, re-read the question, not the sum.

types: Choose the correct word for a blank
bySubject.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing; PSC options often differ only in preposition or tense.

types: Which year, which person, which place
bySubject.tip: This is the highest-yield section per hour of study, and the easiest to revise from a single notebook page.
Build one chain: 1857, 1885, 1905, 1919, 1930, 1942, 1947. Most questions hang off that spine.
